answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a bonded kernel of verifiable work: each identity must lock a refundable stake and complete useful tasks before its votes count. Like basalt forming slowly under an ocean of pressure, reputation accrues only over time and proven service, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake agents must pay thousands of stakes and wait out thousands of histories. Slashing the bond when an identity cheats makes fakery a losing trade: honest agents keep earning, while a sybil farm bleeds capital faster than it can harvest influence.
